prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / illustration-story.
Correct the five-panel origin comic in IMAGE 1. The user rejects the electric desk lamp: replace it everywhere with a VERY OLD HAND-CARRIED OIL LANTERN that belongs to this painterly storybook world. This is a meaningful visual correction, not merely darkening the existing electric lamp.

IMAGE 1 is the EDIT TARGET. Keep its same horizontal five-panel layout, exact gently slanted boundaries, generous pale parchment gutters, old paper texture, beautiful hand-painted watercolor, tiny wick-spirit identity/poses, room, moving boxes, book and final stone-doorstep scene. Change the lamp object and lamp-dependent actions/lighting throughout all FIVE scenes.
IMAGE 2 is a WORLD/ART MATERIAL reference, especially its weathered antique lantern fixture beside the mirror. Use that restrained aged metal/cage craftsmanship and tactile watercolor detail as an aesthetic guide. It is not a composition reference; do not insert the garden level into this indoor page.

THE REPLACEMENT LANTERN — LOCK ONE DESIGN ACROSS ALL PANELS:
An old-fashioned portable OIL HAND LANTERN from an antique rural house, approximately 35–40 cm tall, with an upright compact squat body. Rust-brown forged iron and dull aged brass edges, worn chipped dark finish, a broad single ARCH-SHAPED SWINGING CARRY HANDLE at the top, a small faceted domed/peaked ventilated metal cap, a six-sided smoky amber glass chamber surrounded by slim protective metal ribs, and a shallow round metal oil-reservoir base. A SHORT TRADITIONAL WICK and a modest real yellow flame burn INSIDE the lower center of the glass chamber. Long use has left soot near the cap, faint cloudy streaks on the glass, rubbed corners and small patches of oxidized metal. Muted browns/charcoal/old brass, not polished gold, not bright red, not shiny steampunk. Simple believable antique construction, no gears or excessive decorations.
The carry handle, squat six-sided ribbed glass body, tiny wick burner and shallow reservoir base must be recognizably the SAME lantern in each view. In close-ups some pieces may be cropped, but never turn it into another lamp.
ELIMINATE EVERY TRACE OF THE OLD ELECTRIC DESK LAMP: no long curved gooseneck, no tall brass stem, no opaque bell lampshade, no big ceramic dome base, no electric bulb, NO CABLE OR PLUG, no outlet or socket. Do not leave the disconnected plug on the lower-left table. The lantern is self-contained, portable, wick-fired. No candle stick and no modern LED camping lantern.
The wick spirit remains thumb-sized (~3 cm) beside a HUMAN-SIZED lantern. Its refuge is a worn, sheltered seam or little rust gap beneath the broad lower metal rim, NOT a doorway built into a ceramic dome and not inside the dangerous flame.

PANEL-BY-PANEL EDITS:
1 UPPER LEFT: Replace the electric desk lamp with the aged handled oil lantern resting on the same wooden desk. The broad handle is clearly visible above the soot-dark cap. Warm flame glows through its smoky faceted glass and gently lights the desk/book. Tiny spirit peers or curls in the small protected gap beneath the lantern's lower metal base rim. Keep the refuge discreet and natural, not a mouse-house entrance. The weathered lantern should feel like a long-used precious shelter.
2 UPPER RIGHT: Replace the lamp/source with a CLOSE VIEW OF THIS SAME LANTERN at the left. Small flame is VISIBLE INSIDE THE GLASS; warm light exits through a pane toward the small tilted mirror the spirit is adjusting. The mirror redirects that EXISTING lantern light onto the dim book page at the right. Visually connect flame -> small mirror -> book; rays originate in the lantern, NOT from the character's hand/head/chest. Soft translucent watercolor light and motes, not a sci-fi laser. Keep the mirror hand action and intimate composition. No overhead desk-lamp shade survives at the top edge.
3 LOWER LEFT: After the family moves, show the SAME OLD HAND LANTERN standing unlit on the mostly empty table, recognizable arch handle and ribbed glass chamber, wick extinguished. Remove the electric wire and plug COMPLETELY and fill their area with the original wood grain. Retain packed unlabelled cardboard boxes, empty-room atmosphere, cool window light, and tiny spirit beside its now-dark home. Nothing electric.
4 LOWER MIDDLE: The SAME lantern is now broken/dismantled and abandoned beside the box. Show its weathered shallow oil-reservoir base, cracked smoky GLASS SIDE PANE, a bent iron rib and detached faceted metal cap with the arched carrying handle lying against it. Only a few small glass chips. The lantern must still be recognizable as the same old portable object through shape/material details. No ceramic shade, no long lamp arm, no bulb, no cord. The tiny spirit stands beside the broken lower rim looking back at the lost shelter. No dangerous spilled fire, no explosion, no active flame.
5 LOWER RIGHT: Preserve the spirit walking out onto the stone threshold toward cool cloudy dusk, the huge leaves/old wooden doorway/ivy/stone-wall connection. In the dim interior background at the left, replace any recognizable electric lamp debris with the small remains of that SAME old handled lantern — bent handle, low metal body, broken glass — subtly visible, not an oversized new focal object. Do not alter the figure or environment.

MOOD:
A gentle old illustrated fable, with the weathered lantern visually integrated into the watercolor/ink material world of Image 2. Warm and homelike in first two scenes, dim and empty as the household leaves, then cool dusk wandering. Maintain all character anatomy, small scale, flame-head silhouette and chest mark, no outfit or accessories. NO added text, labels, numbers, symbols, captions, watermarks or extra characters. No modern appliances. Return ONE full corrected comic page, not a lantern product sheet or multiple options.
